hadith:
Al-Adha Festival Sacrifice (Adaahi) - Narrated Al-Bara' bin `Azib:

An uncle of mine called Abu Burda, slaughtered his sacrifice before the `Id prayer. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to him, "Your (slaughtered) sheep was just mutton (not a sacrifice)." Abu Burda said, "O Allah's Apostle! I have got a domestic kid goat." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Slaughter it (as a sacrifice) but it will not be permissible for anybody other than you" The Prophet (ﷺ) added, "Whoever slaughtered his sacrifice before the (`Id) prayer, he only slaughtered for himself, and whoever slaughtered it after the prayer, he offered his sacrifice properly and followed the tradition of the Muslims."
message: Remember that Allah is Al-Qaadir, The Powerful, who has made lawful provisions for you—so enjoy His blessings without guilt or self-deprivation, for this is part of following His wisdom. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) guided us to perform acts of worship at their proper times with sincere intention, approach your daily life with the same consciousness, ensuring your actions align with Allah's guidance rather than merely seeking to please others. Trust in Allah's complete authority and mercy, knowing that obedience comes not through unnecessary hardship, but through balanced living and genuine devotion.
name:
Al Qaadir - الْقَادِرُ - The Powerful

The name Al Qaadir is derived from the Arabic root 'q-d-r', which denotes strength and capability. This name reflects the belief that Allah has complete control over the universe and is capable of exercising His will in all matters. It emphasizes the concept of divine power and authority in Islamic theology.
verse:
At-Tahrim - The Prohibition - 66:1

O Prophet! Why do you prohibit ˹yourself˺ from what Allah has made lawful to you, seeking to please your wives? And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
